claims.summary: Characteristic zero, lambda=3/2. The half-integral cross space H = phi_(+-1)(T) U(eps T) of the cluster degeneration has total finite non-branch weight at most 2M(M-1) for a separated cluster (M>=2) and at most 2M(M-1)-4 with one double root (M>=3), equality iff branch and infinity multiplicities are minimal; the difference is binom(2M,2)-2binom(2M-2,2)+binom(2M-4,2)=4. With the confluent neck hull theorem and eps small, at most 2M-4 non-branch points of H lie beyond the 2M(M-2) neck points. Also: U+zU has orders 0..2M-1 at z=0 iff det Gamma_(M-1)!=0, so the naive node-exponent sum overcounts the confluent neck.
claims.assessment: Working proof by the local-exponent degree count of the confluent criterion; exact Wronskian root count at M=3, eps=1e-12 gives 12 (separated: 6+6 neck) and 8 (confluent: 6 neck + 2 at the cluster scale), all simple.
claims.rationale: Shows that at most 2M-4 of the 2M displaced confluent neck points are non-branch points of the half-integral class, weakening the count tension of the hull entry.
